# SDK naming map

<!-- Generated by scripts/naming_map.py from fern/overrides.yml. Do not edit by hand. -->

How each Trading 212 API operation maps to an SDK method. Upstream `operationId`s are
inconsistent (`orders_1`, `placeStopOrder_1` for stop-limit, `getAll`), so every operation is
renamed in `fern/overrides.yml`. Fern then applies each language's casing convention.

All paths are relative to `/api/v0/equity`.

| Endpoint | Upstream operationId | TypeScript | Python | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /account/summary` | `getAccountSummary` | `client.account.getSummary()` | `client.account.get_summary()` |  |
| `GET /history/dividends` | `dividends` | `client.history.listDividends()` | `client.history.list_dividends()` | paginated¹ |
| `GET /history/orders` | `orders_1` | `client.history.listOrders()` | `client.history.list_orders()` | paginated¹ |
| `GET /history/exports` | `getReports` | `client.history.listReports()` | `client.history.list_reports()` |  |
| `GET /history/transactions` | `transactions` | `client.history.listTransactions()` | `client.history.list_transactions()` | paginated¹ |
| `POST /history/exports` | `requestReport` | `client.history.requestReport()` | `client.history.request_report()` |  |
| `GET /metadata/instruments` | `instruments` | `client.instruments.list()` | `client.instruments.list()` |  |
| `GET /metadata/exchanges` | `exchanges` | `client.instruments.listExchanges()` | `client.instruments.list_exchanges()` |  |
| `DELETE /orders/{id}` | `cancelOrder` | `client.orders.cancel()` | `client.orders.cancel()` |  |
| `GET /orders/{id}` | `orderById` | `client.orders.get()` | `client.orders.get()` |  |
| `GET /orders` | `orders` | `client.orders.list()` | `client.orders.list()` |  |
| `POST /orders/limit` | `placeLimitOrder` | `client.orders.placeLimit()` | `client.orders.place_limit()` |  |
| `POST /orders/market` | `placeMarketOrder` | `client.orders.placeMarket()` | `client.orders.place_market()` |  |
| `POST /orders/stop` | `placeStopOrder_1` | `client.orders.placeStop()` | `client.orders.place_stop()` |  |
| `POST /orders/stop_limit` | `placeStopOrder` | `client.orders.placeStopLimit()` | `client.orders.place_stop_limit()` |  |
| `POST /pies` | `create` | `client.pies.create()` | `client.pies.create()` | deprecated |
| `DELETE /pies/{id}` | `delete` | `client.pies.delete()` | `client.pies.delete()` | deprecated |
| `POST /pies/{id}/duplicate` | `duplicatePie` | `client.pies.duplicate()` | `client.pies.duplicate()` | deprecated |
| `GET /pies/{id}` | `getDetailed` | `client.pies.get()` | `client.pies.get()` | deprecated |
| `GET /pies` | `getAll` | `client.pies.list()` | `client.pies.list()` | deprecated |
| `POST /pies/{id}` | `update` | `client.pies.update()` | `client.pies.update()` | deprecated |
| `GET /positions` | `getPositions` | `client.positions.list()` | `client.positions.list()` |  |

¹ TypeScript methods return an async-iterable `Page` that fetches further pages automatically
(`for await (const item of await client.history.listOrders())`). In Python, wrap the method with
`t212.pagination.paginate` (`for item in paginate(client.history.list_orders)`).
